newsitem.title: USA: PS Enterprise Q1 helped by nuclear cost dip.
newsitem.headline: PS Enterprise Q1 helped by nuclear cost dip.

text.p: Public Service Enterprise Group Inc said first quarter earnings were helped by lower nuclear operating expenses.

Reporting earnings per share of $0.83, compared with $0.79 in 1996's initial three months, the company said it expects the year-to-year comparison to improve, particularly after one unit of the Salem Nuclear Generating Station returns to service later this quarter.
The first quarter earnings per share gain came on fewer shares outstanding as net income declined to $192.8 million from $194.1 million.
The five percent per share increase matched Enterprise Chief Financial Officer Robert C. Murray's February forecast.
But First Call's consensus continued to project unchanged first quarter earnings.

Enterprise said the latest quarter reflected considerably lower nuclear operating expenses incurred by its principal subsidiary, Public Service Electric and Gas Co, which more than offset the impact of warmer winter weather this year and its effect on the utility's gas and electric sales.
The "performance of PSE&G's Hope Creek Nuclear Generating Station, in particular, enabled us to realize the much lower nuclear expenses," said chief executive E. James Ferland.

"Hope Creek was off line for extended maintenance during the first quarter of 1996 but was in service during the entire first quarter of this year." The plant is 95 percent owned by PSE&G and five percent by Atlantic Energy Inc.
Ferland said comparatively lower expenses associated with the refurbishment of the two units at the Salem Nuclear Generating Station also had a positive earnings impact.

"As the year progresses, we expect year-to-year earnings comparisons to improve, particularly after Salem Unit 2 returns to service later this quarter." Salem Unit 1 is scheduled to resume operation in the fall. PSE&G has a 42.6 percent interest in Salem, as does PECO Energy Co. The rest is shared by Atlantic Energy and Delmarva Power and Light Co.

Enterprise said PSE&G's electric sales to customers through March decreased 4.6 percent when compared with 1996 first quarter sales. Residential, commercial and industrial sales were down 5.6 percent, 4.7 percent and 3.4 percent, respectively.

Total gas sold and transported decreased 2.7 percent in the latest quarter of 1997 when compared with the same period in 1996. Residential sales were down 12.3 percent, stemming largely from the warmer weather this year. Firm commercial and firm industrial sales were down 20.2 percent and 14.6 percent, due in part to the weather but also largely to a continuing shift of customers to the transportation service category, which increased 22.9 percent.
